summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer and a history of gastroparesis presented with severe right back pain, right lower extremity weakness, and a painful bullous rash on her right side. She was admitted for evaluation and management, with initial concern for shingles with possible bacterial superinfection, leading to treatment with intravenous vancomycin and Zosyn. MRI of the spine showed extensive metastatic bone disease without cord compression. A clogged G-J tube was successfully replaced with an 18 French tube to prevent recurrent blockages. She improved with pain control, nutritional support, and antibiotic therapy. The liver metastases showed decreased burden on CT, indicating response to prior chemotherapy. She was transitioned back to home pain medications, started on oral vancomycin, and discharged with plans to resume outpatient paclitaxel therapy and home nursing support.
